cards.name: Entropy
cards.summary: Sets the smart object's stack mode to Entropy: each output pixel is the entropy (information content) of that pixel's channel values across all the stacked frames, so areas whose values vary between frames read differently from areas that stay constant. An analysis map rather than a finished look; on a one-layer smart object the harvest run left the layer with empty bounds, since there is no variation to measure.
cards.how: Put the aligned frames inside one smart object first: File > Scripts > Load Files into Stack (tick Attempt to Automatically Align Source Images and Create Smart Object after Loading Layers), or select the layers, run Edit > Auto-Align Layers and Layer > Smart Objects > Convert to Smart Object; then pick the mode. File > Scripts > Statistics does all of it in one step. The mode stays live: switch modes or choose None at any time, and double-click the smart object to edit the frames.
use_for: mapping which areas of a locked-off frame sequence change between shots before deciding what to mask
technical stack analysis (astronomy, microscopy, time-lapse frames) where information content per pixel matters
avoid: removing tourists or noise: use Stack Mode > Median
a smart object holding a single layer: the result is empty
unaligned handheld frames: run Edit > Auto-Align Layers on the frames before converting them to a smart object
cards.script_api: executeAction(stringIDToTypeID('applyImageStackPluginRenderer'), desc, DialogModes.NO) with desc: imageStackPlugin (class) = charIDToTypeID('entr'), name (string) = 'Entropy'; verified live on a smart-object scratch document (history 'Rendering Image Stack Entropy').

cards.name: Kurtosis
cards.summary: Sets the smart object's stack mode to Kurtosis: each output pixel is the kurtosis of that pixel's channel values across the stacked frames, a measure of how peaked or flat their distribution is compared with a normal distribution; pixels that hold steady except for rare outlier frames score high. Produces a statistical map, not a pictorial image; with one layer inside, the harvest run left the layer empty.
cards.how: Put the aligned frames inside one smart object first: File > Scripts > Load Files into Stack (tick Attempt to Automatically Align Source Images and Create Smart Object after Loading Layers), or select the layers, run Edit > Auto-Align Layers and Layer > Smart Objects > Convert to Smart Object; then pick the mode. File > Scripts > Statistics does all of it in one step. The mode stays live: switch modes or choose None at any time, and double-click the smart object to edit the frames.
use_for: flagging pixels where one or two frames deviate sharply from an otherwise steady value (a passing light, a flash) in a fixed-camera stack
scientific or forensic frame-stack analysis
avoid: any design look: use Mean, Median, Maximum or Minimum
fewer than a handful of frames: the statistic is meaningless
unaligned handheld frames: run Edit > Auto-Align Layers on the frames before converting them to a smart object

cards.name: Maximum
cards.summary: Sets the smart object's stack mode to Maximum: every pixel takes the brightest red, green and blue value found in any stacked frame, so bright moving lights accumulate into one image (star trails, light-painting and car light trails, several fireworks or lightning bolts). Channels are chosen independently, so colours can mix from different frames.
cards.how: Put the aligned frames inside one smart object first: File > Scripts > Load Files into Stack (tick Attempt to Automatically Align Source Images and Create Smart Object after Loading Layers), or select the layers, run Edit > Auto-Align Layers and Layer > Smart Objects > Convert to Smart Object; then pick the mode. File > Scripts > Statistics does all of it in one step. The mode stays live: switch modes or choose None at any time, and double-click the smart object to edit the frames.
use_for: star-trail composite from an interval-shot night sky sequence
several fireworks bursts or lightning strikes merged into one hero image
light-painting or traffic light-trail poster from a tripod sequence
avoid: daytime frames with dark moving subjects: the brighter background wins and the subject vanishes; use Median or hand masking
frames of different exposure: the brightest frame dominates; use Mean or Merge to HDR Pro
unaligned handheld frames: run Edit > Auto-Align Layers on the frames before converting them to a smart object

cards.name: Mean
cards.summary: Sets the smart object's stack mode to Mean: each pixel becomes the average of its channel values across all frames, so random noise averages away and anything that moved turns into a translucent blur or ghost, like a long exposure (silky water, smeared crowds) built from many short shots.
cards.how: Put the aligned frames inside one smart object first: File > Scripts > Load Files into Stack (tick Attempt to Automatically Align Source Images and Create Smart Object after Loading Layers), or select the layers, run Edit > Auto-Align Layers and Layer > Smart Objects > Convert to Smart Object; then pick the mode. File > Scripts > Statistics does all of it in one step. The mode stays live: switch modes or choose None at any time, and double-click the smart object to edit the frames.
use_for: simulated long exposure (silky waterfall, smooth sea, blurred crowd) without an ND filter
noise reduction by averaging many identical exposures of a static subject (night city, astro, low-light product)
ghosted motion effect in an architecture or street shot
avoid: removing passers-by cleanly: Mean leaves faint ghosts; use Median
light trails: averaging dims them; use Maximum
unaligned handheld frames: run Edit > Auto-Align Layers on the frames before converting them to a smart object

cards.name: Median
cards.summary: Sets the smart object's stack mode to Median: each pixel takes the middle value of its channels across the frames, so anything present in fewer than half of them (tourists, cars, birds, random noise) disappears and the static scene remains sharp and ghost-free.
cards.how: Put the aligned frames inside one smart object first: File > Scripts > Load Files into Stack (tick Attempt to Automatically Align Source Images and Create Smart Object after Loading Layers), or select the layers, run Edit > Auto-Align Layers and Layer > Smart Objects > Convert to Smart Object; then pick the mode. File > Scripts > Statistics does all of it in one step. The mode stays live: switch modes or choose None at any time, and double-click the smart object to edit the frames.
use_for: empty landmark or street shot from a tripod burst full of passers-by
clean background plate for a composite
noise reduction from a burst with less ghosting than Mean
avoid: a person or car that stays put in most frames: it survives; mask it out by hand
too few frames for the amount of movement: anything present in more than half the frames is kept; shoot more frames
a long-exposure blur look: use Mean
unaligned handheld frames: run Edit > Auto-Align Layers on the frames before converting them to a smart object

File > Scripts > Statistics does all of it in one step. The mode stays live: switch modes or choose None at any time, and double-click the smart object to edit the frames.
use_for: removing bright moving lights or flash pops from a locked-off sequence
stroboscopic multiple-exposure of a dark figure crossing a bright background (skier on snow, silhouette against sky)
avoid: star or light trails: use Maximum
frames of uneven exposure: the darkest frame dominates
unaligned handheld frames: run Edit > Auto-Align Layers on the frames before converting them to a smart object

cards.name: Range
cards.summary: Sets the smart object's stack mode to Range: each pixel becomes the maximum minus the minimum of its channel values across the frames, so static areas go black and anything that changed lights up in proportion to how much it changed: a quick difference or motion map. On a one-layer smart object the harvest run left the layer empty (nothing changed).
cards.how: Put the aligned frames inside one smart object first: File > Scripts > Load Files into Stack (tick Attempt to Automatically Align Source Images and Create Smart Object after Loading Layers), or select the layers, run Edit > Auto-Align Layers and Layer > Smart Objects > Convert to Smart Object; then pick the mode. File > Scripts > Statistics does all of it in one step. The mode stays live: switch modes or choose None at any time, and double-click the smart object to edit the frames.
use_for: finding what moved between frames before masking a composite
checking a stack for misalignment (edges glow where frames do not line up)
avoid: a pictorial result: use Mean, Median, Maximum or Minimum
noisy frames: sensor noise shows up as speckle; Standard Deviation is less sensitive to single outliers
unaligned handheld frames: run Edit > Auto-Align Layers on the frames before converting them to a smart object

cards.name: Skewness
cards.summary: Sets the smart object's stack mode to Skewness: each pixel becomes the skewness of its channel values across the frames, a measure of how lopsided their distribution is around the mean (whether the unusual values sit mostly above or mostly below the typical one). A statistical map for analysis; with one layer inside, the harvest run left the layer empty.
cards.how: Put the aligned frames inside one smart object first: File > Scripts > Load Files into Stack (tick Attempt to Automatically Align Source Images and Create Smart Object after Loading Layers), or select the layers, run Edit > Auto-Align Layers and Layer > Smart Objects > Convert to Smart Object; then pick the mode. File > Scripts > Statistics does all of it in one step. The mode stays live: switch modes or choose None at any time, and double-click the smart object to edit the frames.
use_for: telling apart pixels hit by occasional brighter events from those hit by occasional darker ones in a fixed-camera stack
scientific frame-stack analysis
avoid: any design look: use Mean, Median, Maximum or Minimum
unaligned handheld frames: run Edit > Auto-Align Layers on the frames before converting them to a smart object

cards.name: Standard Deviation
cards.summary: Sets the smart object's stack mode to Standard Deviation: each pixel becomes the square root of the variance of its channel values across the frames, so steady areas stay dark and areas that fluctuate brighten with the typical size of the change; a smoother motion map than Range, less driven by a single outlier frame. With one layer inside, the harvest run left the layer empty.
cards.how: Put the aligned frames inside one smart object first: File > Scripts > Load Files into Stack (tick Attempt to Automatically Align Source Images and Create Smart Object after Loading Layers), or select the layers, run Edit > Auto-Align Layers and Layer > Smart Objects > Convert to Smart Object; then pick the mode. File > Scripts > Statistics does all of it in one step. The mode stays live: switch modes or choose None at any time, and double-click the smart object to edit the frames.
use_for: motion or flicker map of a locked-off sequence
judging how noisy or how well aligned a burst is before stacking it
avoid: a pictorial result: use Mean or Median
unaligned handheld frames: run Edit > Auto-Align Layers on the frames before converting them to a smart object

cards.name: Summation
cards.summary: Sets the smart object's stack mode to Summation: each pixel becomes the sum of its channel values across all frames, so every frame adds its light like an additive multiple exposure; the result brightens fast and clips to white unless the frames are dark.
cards.how: Put the aligned frames inside one smart object first: File > Scripts > Load Files into Stack (tick Attempt to Automatically Align Source Images and Create Smart Object after Loading Layers), or select the layers, run Edit > Auto-Align Layers and Layer > Smart Objects > Convert to Smart Object; then pick the mode. File > Scripts > Statistics does all of it in one step. The mode stays live: switch modes or choose None at any time, and double-click the smart object to edit the frames.
use_for: building up brightness from several very dark, underexposed frames (faint night sky, dim light painting)
additive multiple-exposure look from dark frames
avoid: normally exposed frames: they blow out to white; use Mean or Maximum
unaligned handheld frames: run Edit > Auto-Align Layers on the frames before converting them to a smart object

cards.name: Variance
cards.summary: Sets the smart object's stack mode to Variance: each pixel becomes the variance of its channel values across the frames (the squared spread around their mean), so the gap between small and large changes is exaggerated more than with Standard Deviation and small fluctuations drop toward black. With one layer inside, the harvest run left the layer empty.
cards.how: Put the aligned frames inside one smart object first: File > Scripts > Load Files into Stack (tick Attempt to Automatically Align Source Images and Create Smart Object after Loading Layers), or select the layers, run Edit > Auto-Align Layers and Layer > Smart Objects > Convert to Smart Object; then pick the mode. File > Scripts > Statistics does all of it in one step. The mode stays live: switch modes or choose None at any time, and double-click the smart object to edit the frames.
use_for: isolating only the strongest changes in a fixed-camera sequence (big movement, not sensor noise)
statistical frame-stack analysis
avoid: a gentler, proportional change map: use Standard Deviation
any design look: use Mean or Median
unaligned handheld frames: run Edit > Auto-Align Layers on the frames before converting them to a smart object

cards.name: Current Path

Needs a selected path; the harvest made a work path from a rectangular selection and the layer gained a vector mask cropped to it.

masking an image into a custom shape (badge, rounded card, logo outline) that stays editable
print cut-outs that must stay crisp when enlarged
avoid: hair, fur or soft edges: use a pixel layer mask (Select and Mask, Select Subject)
no path selected: the command is disabled; draw one with the Pen tool or make a work path from a selection first
